84Ocean civilization program

Build civilization where the map is still blue.

Thirty-seven anchors, each built for roughly 65,000–70,000 people—about 2.4–2.6 million residents, tourists, and workers across the network. One roaming fleet of 13 million HEAR-TS capsule units moves people, power, water and help, and measures success by whether the living ocean thrives.

01 / Premise

The ocean is not empty space.

Project 84 is a working proposal for a distributed ocean civilization: permanent hubs supported by mobile infrastructure, built around the needs of people and the species already living there.

“Whatever the whales require to live is the purpose, until they tell us otherwise.”
The cetacean covenant · current project doctrine
Hubs and fleet

The hubs are harbor, maintenance and coordination. The HEAR-TS capsules are the ocean-wide working fleet.

Abundance by design

Capacity is deliberately oversized, so power, water, transport and shelter are available before crisis arrives.

The plan is the list

Unknowns stay visible. If the engineering, legal or ecological case is not solved, it remains labeled open.

Built with Project 42

The land-city program trains the trades. The ocean program hires them. Each can stand alone; together they form a pipeline.

02 / The system

Not one city. A living chain.

Every layer has a job. The anchors concentrate capability; the fleet distributes it; the ecology sets the limits.

37

A distributed network of hubs, each serving roughly 65,000–70,000 people: build, repair, coordinate and receive.

Living ocean

The thing the machinery serves—not scenery around the machinery.

Phase one starts with a working rig.Housing takes the platform perimeter, sheltering a central courtyard while the cranes, helipad and working core stay in service.
03 / The fleet

A lifeboat that works every day.

The capsules are the HEAR-TS: one fleet of 13 million standardized units, not two separate systems. At roughly 128 people per capsule in emergency shelter mode, the fleet’s theoretical lifeboat ceiling is about 1.7 billion people. The useful idea is a HEAR-TS capsule that changes roles instead of sitting idle.

15 × 10

meters · one modular HEAR-TS capsule

A pill-shaped hull with a role-specific hardware bay and enough remaining volume for cargo, shelter, research or operations.

  • Design life50 years
  • Hardware reserve30%
  • Usable interior≈641 m³
  • Emergency shelter≈128 people
  • Idle ruleMake hydrogen
  • Primary roleTransport

Move

Passengers, freight, mobile docks and shore handoffs. HEAR-TS capsule for transit; raft for work.

Make

Power, freshwater and hydrogen. Spare capacity turns into useful output instead of waste.

Respond

Call-ahead disaster support: shelter, water, power, communications and coastal logistics.

Restore

Aquaculture, hydrophones, survey work and an iron-fertilization pilot with explicit stop rules.

04 / Roadmap

Build, recognize, consolidate, repeat.

The public campaign and the engineering program run in parallel. A pause after the first diplomatic circuit is part of the plan, not lost momentum.

Now

Prove the loop

Run the small iron pilot. Measure the bloom. Validate stop rules, biomass accounting and whale-aware controls.

First circuit

Twenty stops

Begin with Pacific and ocean states, continue through Asia, then close with larger diplomatic targets.

Then

Three-month gap

Consolidate any recognition, seat chairs, refine legal work and let the story travel before the continental round.

Afterward

Continental tour

One capital per continent, with the Antarctic anchor itself serving as Antarctica’s embassy.

05 / Open holes
23

Unsolved machines.

The plan is honest only if its failure points remain visible. Tap a line to read the current problem.

07Production ramp known issue+

Reaching millions of standardized HEAR-TS capsules per year requires a distributed industrial system beyond anything shipyards currently do at this format.

08Shell engineering known issue+

The 5 mm steel shell is an arbitrary starting point. Fatigue, corrosion, role depth and wooden internal structure all need specialist design and destructive testing.

22The trust charter+

The founder’s intent is clear; enforceable governance over decades is not. The trust needs real jurisdiction, succession rules and independent restraint.

25Legal vehicle+

International waters are not a law-free zone. Flag-state, coastal, environmental and treasury regimes still apply, and the legal architecture remains under review.

The Moon comes later.

Project 84 is the ocean rung in a much longer ladder: Earth, Luna, Jupiter, Alpha Centauri. The ocean program learns how to build distributed civilization before the same question is asked in vacuum.

Ask the founder in 2046.That is when the lunar-city chapter is supposed to stop being “later.”
